ely-thomas-poteau-1920-08-09.A2:
"I'LL SEND YOU TO HELL" NEGRO TOLD POTEAU FARMER AS HE OPENED FIRE
Poteau, Okla., Aug. 9.—A mob which formed here this morning intent upon taking Ely Thomas, negro, from the Le Flore county jail, found upon going to the jail, that he had been removed in the night to Sallisaw, by Sheriff Fred Carter.

Thomas is alleged to have shot Selma Mayfield, 21 years old, a farmer, as he attempted to pass a negro picnic at Calhoun, a small town 10 miles west of here. Saturday.

According to the report to officers, the negro stepped out into the road, as Mayfield approached on horseback and asked where he was going.

"I'm going to hell, if I don't pray more," Mayfield is said to have replied, jokingly.

"I'm going to send you to hell right now," Thomas is alleged to have said.

Without another word, he is alleged to have whipped out a .45 calibre revolver and opened fire on Mayfield. The firstb ulet hit Mayfield in the right leg and as he slid off his horse, the negro is said to have shot a second time, the bullet piercing the horse's neck and lodging in Mayfield's abdomen.

Mayfield started to run with the negro after him, but fell and as Thomas raised the gun for another shot, other negro members of the picnic party caught him and disarmed him. They then called the sheriff. Mayfield is being given medical care here, and it is believed he will live.
ely-thomas-poteau-1920-08-09.A3:
NEGROES IN CLOSE CALL AT POTEAU
Infuriated Mob From Calhoun Is Frustrated From Double Lynching by Activity of LeFlore County Authorities.
Poteau, Ok., Aug. 9. — Instant and decisive action on the part of LeFlore county authorities prevented the lynching of Tim Zachary and Ely Thomas, both negroes, here today by an infuriated mob of citizens who came here at 9 o'clock this morning from Calhoun for the purpose of "stringing up" the two accused men. Both negroes were spirited away from the LeFlore county jail in automobiles and lodged in the state penitentiary at McAlester.

Thomas is alleged to have shot and killed Selma Mayfield, 21 years old, a farmer, as he attempted to pass a negro picnic gathering at Calhoun, a small mining town ten miles west of here Saturday. Zachary is charged with having attempted to attack a 16-year-old daughter of a farmer living near Calhoun. The negro was apprehended after he had overpowered the girl early Monday morning.

Following the alleged criminal actions shown by the negroes in the Calhoun section which it is asserted started with a negro picnic Saturday, citizens of Calhoun held a mass meeting and voted to come to Poteau and "string up" the two men. The mob on its arrival here first paraded the streets and urged others to join it. While the parade was in progress Sheriff Carter and Chief Deputy D. G. Lane, assisted by other deputies sworn in on the spot, went to the ramshackle county jail, via back alleys and contrived to get the two frightened men into automobiles. A drive of 15 miles to the Rock Island railroad was made in record time and the two negroes were later placed in the penitentiary for safekeeping.

Members of the mob learned of the ruse played by the officers and altho they were disappointed, made no attempt to follow the officers, who had a 30-minute lead.

According to reports received here, Thomas stepped out into the road at the picnic ground as Mayfield approached on horseback and asked where he was going.

"I'm going to hell if I don't play more," Mayfield is said to have replied jokingly.

"I'm going to send you to hell right now," Thomas is alleged to have said.

Without another word he is alleged to have whipped out a 45-calibre revolver and opened fire on Mayfield. The first bullet hit Mayfield in the right leg and as he slid off his horse the negro is said to have shot a second time, the bullet piercing the horse's neck and lodging in Mayfield's abdomen.

Mayfield started to run with the negro after him, but fell and as Thomas raised the gun for another shot, other negro members of the picnic party caught him and disarmed him. They summoned the sheriff.

Mob Forms When Negro is Convicted
Poteau, Okla., Sept. 4.—Ely Thomas, negro, was found guilty of murder in district court here today and sentenced to be electrocuted. The negro was charged with having killed Selma Mayfield, white farmer living near Calhoun, August 7.

The sentence was imposed by a jury.

The shooting occured at a picnic near Calhoun, where the negro is alleged to have stepped into the road and shot Mayfield as he was riding past on horseback.

The negro was taken to the Poteau jail after the shooting, where a mob of citizens formed. The negro was taken out of town by officers when the mob threatened violence.

DEATH SENTENCE FOR
Poteau, Okla., Sept. 9.—The death sentence was imposed upon Ely Thomas by a jury here Saturday, which found him guilty of the murder of Selma Mayfield, a white farmer, near Calhoun, Okla., August 7. Thomas was brought here following the shooting and later removed from town when a mob gathered about the jail and threatened violence.

ely-thomas-poteau-1920-08-09.A9:
WILL HE BE PARDONED?
Case of Murderer Checked Up to a Governor; Death Penalty Due in November
Oklahoma City, Sept. 18-The fate
in November
Oklahoma City, Sept. 18.—The fate of Eli Thomas of Calhoun, sentenced to be electrocuted at McAlester, Nov. 23, for the murder of Selma Mayfield, was placed in the hands of Governor Robertson today. A complete transcript of evidence in the case was received by the governor and sent to the criminal court of appeals for review.
Thomas was convicted in the district court of LeFlore county on Sept. 4. on a charge of shooting Mayfield, at a picnic near Calhoun on August 6.

james-jackson-kinston-1920-08-05.A2:
Pythians Report Shows Big Gains During the Year
SVILLE, O., August 2.—The O. H. Lodge, Colored Knights of Pythia, evening in this city last week, big success in every way, and all officers were highly entertained by General K. of P.'s and citizens. One outstanding features of the meet were the masterly address deliverer, Grand Chancellor Robert B. Barclay, Columbus, in response to the address of welcome by the mayor of the city. He made a powerful plea for justice for, and a stirring defense of the race, and pointed out that of the thousands who entered the World War, more than 10,000 were Colored Pythians. He said: "If the Colored men in the South were given fair play and equal opportunity for education and development, and if laws were passed applying equally to white and Colored alike, and if the race could secure justice in the courts we would be regarded more as law-abiding citizens than as criminals." Reports made showed an amazing growth in the order in Ohio, during Grand Chancelor Barcus' administration. During the year 1967 new members were added to the order; 177 reinstated, making a total gain in membership for the year of 2,144. The receipts for the year totaled for the insurance department, $30,028.95, and expenditures $24,281.00, leaving a balance of $5,667.95, a gain over the preceding year. The total amount of investment of insurance funds, and resources of the order, on July 1st, amounted to $30,045.86. The following officers were elected for the ensuing year: Grand Chancelor, Robert B. Barcus, Columbus; Granr Vice/Chancelor, Wm. H. Ferguson, Columbus; Grand Prelate, L. W. White, Rendville; Grand Keeper of Records and Seal, John W. Harris, Columbus; Grand Master of Exchequer, Henry M. Higgins, Cincinnati; Grand Med. Reg., Joseph C. Bradfield, Lima; Grand Attorney, W. leroy-mitchell-alton-1920-08.A3:
Slays Assailant of Sister.
[By Associated Press]
Sinys Assallat of Siste
[By Associated Press.]
NVILLE, VA. august 14

DANVILLE, VA., August 14.—A few hours after attempting to attack a white girl near Alton, Halifax County, Leroy Mitchell, negro, was shot and killed by the young woman's brother, according to a report reaching here today. Trailed by a posse and caught, Mitchell showed fight with an ax when cornered, the girl's brother firing a load from a shotgun into the negro's stomach. Mitchell died shortly after being carried to the Houston jail.
leroy-mitchell-alton-1920-08.A4:
SHOTGUNWOUNDSFATALTO NEGRO
Danville, Va., Aug. 1. — Leroy Mitchell, a South Carolina negro, died at Halifax County jail today from the effects of shotgun wounds through the body, received when he tried to elude a posse of farmers who started on his trail after an attempted assault, it is alleged, on Miss Mattie Ramsey, of Alton. The girl's screams brought help.
